name: Reuel
title: Midianite priest and Moses' father-in-law
summary: Reuel, also known as Jethro, was a Midianite priest who became Moses' father-in-law. He welcomed Moses when he fled from Egypt and gave him his daughter Zipporah in marriage. He played an important advisory role for Moses during the Israelites' wilderness journey, especially in organizing the judicial system.

keyEvents.title: Moses flees to Midian and meets Reuel
keyEvents.description: After killing an Egyptian, Moses fled to Midian, where he helped Reuel's daughters at the well. Reuel welcomed Moses and gave him his daughter Zipporah in marriage.

keyEvents.title: Reuel gives his daughter Zipporah to Moses
keyEvents.description: Reuel gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses as a wife, and she bore him a son named Gershom.

keyEvents.title: Moses as shepherd with Reuel
keyEvents.description: Moses tended his father-in-law Jethro's (Reuel) small livestock, the priest of Midian, and led the flock to the back of the wilderness where he met God at the burning bush.

keyEvents.title: Jethro (Reuel) visits Moses in the wilderness
keyEvents.description: After leaving Egypt, Jethro came to Moses in the wilderness with Zipporah and her sons, rejoicing over all that the Lord had done for Israel. He offered sacrifices to God.

keyEvents.title: Reuel's advice on the judicial system
keyEvents.description: Jethro (Reuel) advised Moses to appoint judges over the people to lighten his burden, so that only the most difficult cases were brought before Moses. Moses followed his father-in-law's counsel.

keyEvents.title: Reuel's descendants mentioned among the Edomites
keyEvents.description: In Esau's genealogy, Reuel is named as a son of Esau and Bashemath, with several sons who became tribal chiefs in Edom. This is a different Reuel than Moses' father-in-law.
